channel.title: Crypto Readout
channel.description: Crypto Readout reports on Bitcoin, Ethereum and altcoin markets, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, network upgrades and crypto regulation worldwide.

item.title: Chainflip swaps: how to diagnose a pending transfer
item.description: A pending swap can mean the deposit is confirming, awaiting validator witnessing, waiting for execution, or queued for payout; trace the stage before acting.

item.title: What a Cross-Chain Swap Costs Before the Tokens Arrive
item.description: A cross-chain swap can charge for execution on both networks, routing and liquidity; compare the quoted output, price protection and failure terms before sending.

item.title: How LPs Can Measure Correlated-Asset Depeg Exposure
item.description: A depeg can turn a market-neutral pool into a one-sided position; LPs can assess exposure by tracing asset links, pool mechanics and exit liquidity.

item.title: What a Solana Swap Signature Authorizes
item.description: A Solana swap signature authorizes a specific transaction message, so check the route, token movement, slippage limit and any extra permissions before approving it.

item.title: Byreal: When to Swap and When to Supply Liquidity
item.description: A swap exchanges one token for another; concentrated liquidity can earn trading fees, but price ranges change your exposure and add inventory risk.

item.title: When Is a Cross-Chain Transfer Settled?
item.description: A cross-chain transfer is settled only when the destination chain records the expected asset or call; verify both sides and the bridge’s final status.

item.title: Read a Token’s Trading History Before You Swap
item.description: A token’s trading history shows where swaps happened, how liquidity and price moved, and which pool, route and transaction details to verify before you swap.

item.title: Five Checks for Slippage on Volatile Avalanche Swaps
item.description: On Avalanche, set slippage against the route and minimum output: compare quotes, check liquidity and volatility, then use the smallest buffer likely to execute.

item.title: A pool prompt can grant more than a swap
item.description: A pool prompt may request token allowance or a signed permit; check the spender, token, amount and chain, then approve only the access your trade needs.

item.title: Check Token Balances Before You Deposit Into a Pool
item.description: Check the network, token contracts, spendable balances and pool ratio before approving a deposit, so you know what will be used and what must stay in your wallet.

item.title: How Base swap trading and liquidity work on Base
item.description: A Base swap uses an automated market maker to exchange tokens or pool them for trading; learn the transaction steps, LP trade-offs and checks.

item.title: How Cryptographic Precompiles Use Energy
item.description: Cryptographic precompiles run fixed routines inside a blockchain virtual machine; the chain’s pricing rules determine the gas or energy each call consumes.

item.title: Why TRON Energy Takes Time to Reach Your Wallet
item.description: TRON Energy is delegated on-chain, so payment, transaction inclusion and wallet refresh happen in separate steps; learn which delay matters and when to retry.

item.title: Estimating Energy for a USDT TRC-20 Transfer
item.description: Estimate a USDT transfer by simulating its exact contract call, then account for available Energy, Bandwidth and the fee limit before you send it.

item.title: Why XMR Bridge Swaps Take Time
item.description: An XMR swap can wait on source-chain confirmations, Monero settlement or provider liquidity; identify the stage before changing routes, retrying or sending funds again.

item.title: The real cost of an XMR-to-BTC swap
item.description: An XMR-to-BTC swap costs more than its displayed fee: compare the exchange rate, both networks’ transaction fees and any provider charge against the final BTC received.

item.title: How Many Monero Confirmations Should You Wait For?
item.description: For Monero, wait for 10 confirmations before treating ordinary wallet funds as spendable; deposit services set their own thresholds, so check their rules.

item.title: How to Use PooCoin to Track and Trade BSC Tokens
item.description: Tracking a BSC token starts with its contract address; trading adds a liquidity pool, swap quote and wallet approval, each of which needs a separate check.

item.title: Blackhole swap: How to Price an Avalanche Trade
item.description: A swap quote is an estimate, not a guaranteed fill: check the token pair, network, route and slippage before approving an Avalanche transaction.

item.title: How to Pay Gas When Swapping Tokens on Arbitrum
item.description: On Arbitrum One, swaps use ETH for network gas; learn what the wallet charges, why approvals can cost extra, and how to fund a trade before you swap.
